A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProtoTS and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched across pagination changes, figure revisions, and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, ablations, a 12-participant interpretability study in Table 4, and an expert-steering case study in Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the forecasting experiments and reports a 24-participant interpretability study, revised user-study results, and training-time measurements in Table 9.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an automatic rule for selecting leaves for further splitting: accumulate instance MAE over top-k matching leaves, normalize by assignment count, and select the highest-loss fraction. Equation 9 also reverses the entropy term's sign and introduces its weight, lambda. These refine the retained architecture; the PDFs do not establish that the retained forecasting experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four LOF regions, five EPF markets, and six multivariate benchmarks in Appendix G. The user-study task and represented population are not reported as changing; its increased participant count is a sample-size change.

E2.justification: Corresponding forecasting, interpretability, and sensitivity experiments retain their comparator sets and baseline adaptations. The new timing table reuses TimeXer, iTransformer, and TiDE, which were already evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 increases the reported user-study sample from 12 to 24 participants while retaining the questions, metrics, and randomized presentation. The new timing comparison reports matched hardware, optimizer, learning rate, sequence length, and batch size. Existing forecasting windows and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, prototype-count and training-data sensitivity analyses, expert-steering case study, and forecast visualizations retain the same evidence. The new timing table adds comparative cost measurements without introducing an additional ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports UPrec with ± values of 3.6%, 3.4%, and 2.8% for ProtoTS, TFT, and NBEATSx. Their meaning and estimation procedure are not specified. The existing five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Appendix C.3 and the five-seed expert-edit result remain unchanged.

E6.justification: With the user-study sample increasing from 12 to 24, Table 4 retains ProtoTS UPrec at 77%, changes TFT from 69% to 64%, and NBEATSx from 59% to 62%. Their respective SUS scores change from 71.72/26.82/31.92 to 73.36/29.74/38.66. These are different-sample results. New Table 9 reports 40.8/19.5/12.5/11.1 ms per iteration for ProtoTS/TimeXer/iTransformer/TiDE. Forecasting and ablation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 9 changes the regularizer from positive sum f log f to negative lambda times that sum. For positive lambda, this corrects the inconsistency between minimizing the stated loss and encouraging concentrated prototype weights. Algorithm 1 also defines a normalized per-leaf loss score; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core claims about forecasting accuracy, hierarchical global and local explanations, expert steering, and the LOF dataset contribution. The headline forecasting improvements and novelty positioning are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds computational overhead as a limitation and attributes the higher training time to multi-channel embedding and hierarchical prototype computations. The limitations concerning irregular patterns and dependence on domain experts, together with existing result interpretations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds operational splitting pseudocode and training-time information, although values for lambda, k, and alpha remain unspecified. Appendix B.1 removes LOF's exact date range, 2022-02-01 to 2025-02-13, and its provincial Chinese simulation context, replacing the dates with 'three years.' Other implementation and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and comparisons with prior forecasting, interpretability, and prototype methods. The claimed novelty of decoding prototypes into forecast sequences is unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized: v3 expands the splitting explanation, corrects fusion-order prose to match unchanged Equation 3, clarifies transpose notation, and changes 'non-leaf' to 'leaf.' It also shortens dataset wording and removes the conference-publication header. The overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with revised typography, arrows, and corrected illustrative weights. v3 adds the Algorithm 1 display and timing Table 9, and Table 4 gains uncertainty formatting. Existing figures and tables shift with pagination; the former Tables 9 and 10 become Tables 10 and 11.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation 9 resolves a mismatch with the stated concentration objective, and Algorithm 1 makes leaf selection explicit. The larger user study and new training-cost measurements improve empirical reporting. Gains are limited by undefined UPrec uncertainty values, unspecified new hyperparameter values, and removal of precise LOF provenance and dates. The core forecasting evidence remains unchanged.
